summary: mTLS client certificate chain truncated by customer egress proxy causing control-plane auth failures on private deployment
description:
Issue summary:
Customer BrightMetrics reported intermittent control-plane authentication failures from their private deployment. Calls from the customer agents to Redwood control-plane started failing TLS mTLS verification after a firewall/egress gateway change on their side.

Impact:
- Control-plane heartbeats from fleet agents bounce with mTLS errors, causing short-lived registration losses and transient task scheduling failures.
- Affects ~12 agents across two dedicated subnets. No model-serving requests were affected directly, but agent reconnections caused short scheduling delays.

Environment:
- Private deployment (customer-managed VPC)
- prod-us-west region (us-west-2)
- Control-plane endpoint: cp-prod.redwood-internal.example.net
- Customer egress sits behind a corporate TLS-terminating gateway/proxy (appliance vendor: SquidCorp v4.1)

Observed at: 2026-03-10 07:43 UTC
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Customer deploys agent with pinned control-plane cert verification enabled.
2) Egress gateway performs outbound TLS termination/inspection and re-initiates TLS to control-plane.
3) Agents attempt mTLS auth; control-plane rejects handshake with client-chain errors.

Note: Reproducible when gateway is on path; bypassing gateway (direct internet egress) makes the problem disappear.
logs:
[control-plane] 2026-03-10T07:43:12Z ERROR auth: client handshake failed: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority
[agent-17] 2026-03-10T07:43:12Z WARN heartbeat: control-plane rejected connection: client cert chain incomplete
[tcpdump] TLS ClientHello shows SNI: cp-prod.redwood-internal.example.net, ALPN: h2
[proxy-inspect] Re-originated TLS to cp-prod.redwood-internal.example.net; forwarded client cert length: 0 bytes (expected ~2.1KB)
investigation_notes:
- Initial hypothesis: corporate proxy is terminating mTLS and not forwarding the full client certificate chain, or it is stripping TLS client cert info when re-establishing TLS.
- Collected packet captures at agent and gateway; capture shows agent sends full client certificate chain in TLS ClientAuth, but the gateway's re-originated connection omits client cert (gateway performs TLS termination and re-init).
- Control-plane logs show 'x509: certificate signed by unknown authority' followed by 'client cert chain incomplete'.
- Customer confirmed a recent gateway firmware update that enabled 'certificate rewriting' for outbound TLS inspection.
- Reproduction verified by toggling gateway to TCP pass-through mode: when pass-through is enabled control-plane auth succeeds immediately.
- Created internal INT-4451 to track engineering follow-up on control-plane behavior when client certs are absent/trimmed by middleboxes.
resolution_notes:
Workaround implemented: BrightMetrics reverted the gateway setting to preserve client cert information by enabling TLS passthrough for control-plane hostnames and whitelisting cp-prod.redwood-internal.example.net. After change, all agents re-registered and heartbeats stabilized.

Permanent guidance provided to customer:
- Configure egress proxy to either: 1) perform TCP passthrough for mTLS endpoints, or 2) if TLS inspection is required, configure the proxy to re-inject the original client certificate chain (some appliances support 'forward client cert' or 'proxy-cert-forwarding').
- Add control-plane hostnames to proxy whitelist where mTLS is required.

Internal follow-up:
- INT-4451 assigned to infra-auth team to harden control-plane error messaging and provide clearer telemetry when client certs are absent.
- Add a KB entry in runbook: 'Detecting and mitigating client cert truncation by egress proxies'.
